title: OSHA crane signals study guide
description: Crane signals study guide: when a signal person is required, hand, voice, audible and new signals, lost signals, stops, multiple cranes (29 CFR 1926.1419).
intro: 29 CFR 1926.1419 sets the general requirements for signals in OSHA's construction crane and derrick standard (Subpart CC). This guide sets out what the federal rule text states on when a signal person must be provided, the types of signals allowed, the Standard Method and non-standard hand signals, new signals and the conditions the employer must demonstrate for them, suitability for site conditions, what the operator must do when the signal link is interrupted or a safety problem arises, the stop or emergency stop signal, direction perspective, and signaling more than one crane/derrick. Related definitions come from 1926.1401, with the signal-related provisions of 1926.1417 and the communication duties in 1926.1424. Hand-signal charts are not described here. goraedu does not certify operators or signal persons, and this is not a certification exam. Your State may run its own OSHA-approved plan with its own rules, so check them too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

topics.name: When a signal person is required

points.text: 1926.1419(a) lists three situations, and a signal person must be provided in each of them.
points.quote: A signal person must be provided in each of the following situations:

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One situation is when the point of operation is not in full view of the operator. The rule says the point of operation means the load travel or the area near or at load placement.
points.quote: The point of operation, meaning the load travel or the area near or at load placement, is not in full view of the operator.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A second situation applies when the equipment is traveling: a signal person is required when the view in the direction of travel is obstructed.
points.quote: When the equipment is traveling, the view in the direction of travel is obstructed.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A third situation is when, due to site specific safety concerns, either the operator or the person handling the load determines that a signal person is necessary.
points.quote: Due to site specific safety concerns, either the operator or the person handling the load determines that it is necessary.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: In Subpart CC, "operator" means a person who is operating the equipment.
points.quote: Operator means a person who is operating the equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The qualification requirements for signal persons (§ 1926.1428) are outside the sections we hold and are not set out here.

topics.name: Types of signals and hand signals

points.text: Signals to operators must be by hand, voice, audible, or new signals.
points.quote: Signals to operators must be by hand, voice, audible, or new signals.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: An audible signal is a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds; the definition gives a bell, horn, or whistle as examples, without limiting it to them.
points.quote: Audible signal means a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds. Examples include, but are not limited to, sounds made by a bell, horn, or whistle.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The "Standard Method" is defined as the protocol in appendix A of Subpart CC for hand signals.
points.quote: Standard Method means the protocol in appendix A of this subpart for hand signals.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When hand signals are used, the Standard Method must be used.
points.quote: When using hand signals, the Standard Method must be used (see appendix A of this subpart).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Exception: non-standard hand signals may be used, in accordance with 1926.1419(c)(2), where use of the Standard Method is infeasible.
points.quote: Exception: Where use of the Standard Method for hand signals is infeasible, or where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used in accordance with paragraph (c)(2) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The same exception covers an operation or use of an attachment that is not covered in the Standard Method.
points.quote: where an operation or use of an attachment is not covered in the Standard Method, non-standard hand signals may be used

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: "Attachments" means any device that expands the range of tasks that can be done by the equipment; the definition gives an auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver and boom-attached personnel platform as examples.
points.quote: Attachments means any device that expands the range of tasks that can be done by the equipment. Examples include, but are not limited to: An auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver, and boom-attached personnel platform.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: The hand-signal chart in appendix A is not described or reproduced here.

topics.name: Non-standard hand signals and new signals

points.text: When non-standard hand signals are used, the signal person, the operator and the lift director (where there is one) must contact each other before the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used.
points.quote: When using non-standard hand signals, the signal person, operator, and lift director (where there is one) must contact each other prior to the operation and agree on the non-standard hand signals that will be used.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The lift director is part of that agreement only where there is one.
points.quote: lift director (where there is one)

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: New signals are signals other than hand, voice, or audible signals. They may be used where the employer demonstrates that one of the two conditions in 1926.1419(d) is met.
points.quote: Signals other than hand, voice, or audible signals may be used where the employer demonstrates that:

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option: the new signals provide at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals.
points.quote: The new signals provide at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals, or

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The other option: the new signals comply with a national consensus standard that provides at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals.
points.quote: The new signals comply with a national consensus standard that provides at least equally effective communication as voice, audible, or Standard Method hand signals.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The duty to demonstrate that new signals qualify falls on the employer.
points.quote: may be used where the employer demonstrates that

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Suitability and keeping the signal link

points.text: Both the signals used (hand, voice, audible, or new) and the means of transmitting them to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, radio, etc.) must be appropriate for the site conditions.
points.quote: The signals used (hand, voice, audible, or new), and means of transmitting the signals to the operator (such as direct line of sight, video, radio, etc.), must be appropriate for the site conditions.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: In Subpart CC, "such as" means "such as, but not limited to", so the listed means of transmitting signals are examples.
points.quote: Such as means “such as, but not limited to.”

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: During operations requiring signals, the ability to transmit signals between the operator and signal person must be maintained.
points.quote: During operations requiring signals, the ability to transmit signals between the operator and signal person must be maintained.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If that ability is interrupted at any time, the operator must safely stop operations requiring signals. They stay stopped until the ability is reestablished and a proper signal is given and understood.
points.quote: If that ability is interrupted at any time, the operator must safely stop operations requiring signals until it is reestablished and a proper signal is given and understood.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A dedicated channel is a line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick, or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s).
points.quote: Dedicated channel means a line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: While actually operating the equipment, the operator must not engage in any practice or activity that diverts his/her attention, such as using cellular phones, other than when they are used for signal communications.
points.quote: The operator must not engage in any practice or activity that diverts his/her attention while actually engaged in operating the equipment, such as the use of cellular phones (other than when used for signal communications).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1417, Operation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If the operator becomes aware of a safety problem and needs to communicate with the signal person, the operator must safely stop operations.
points.quote: If the operator becomes aware of a safety problem and needs to communicate with the signal person, the operator must safely stop operations.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Operations must not resume until the operator and signal person agree that the problem has been resolved.
points.quote: Operations must not resume until the operator and signal person agree that the problem has been resolved.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must alert the operator or signal person by giving the stop or emergency stop signal.
points.quote: Anyone who becomes aware of a safety problem must alert the operator or signal person by giving the stop or emergency stop signal.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: 1926.1419(j) carries a note pointing to 1926.1417(y), which requires the operator to obey a stop or emergency stop signal.
points.quote: (NOTE: § 1926.1417(y) requires the operator to obey a stop or emergency stop signal).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The operator must obey a stop (or emergency stop) signal, irrespective of who gives it.
points.quote: The operator must obey a stop (or emergency stop) signal, irrespective of who gives it.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1417, Operation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Who signals, direction and multiple cranes

points.text: Only one person may give signals to a crane/derrick at a time, except in the circumstances covered by 1926.1419(j).
points.quote: Only one person may give signals to a crane/derrick at a time, except in circumstances covered by paragraph (j) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: All directions the signal person gives the operator must be given from the operator's direction perspective.
points.quote: All directions given to the operator by the signal person must be given from the operator's direction perspective.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Where a signal person (or persons) is in communication with more than one crane/derrick, a system must be used for identifying the crane/derrick each signal is for.
points.quote: Where a signal person(s) is in communication with more than one crane/derrick, a system must be used for identifying the crane/derrick each signal is for

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: One option for that system: for each signal, before giving the function/direction, the signal person identifies the crane/derrick the signal is for.
points.quote: for each signal, prior to giving the function/direction, the signal person must identify the crane/ derrick the signal is for, or

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The other option: the signal person uses an equally effective method of identifying which crane/derrick the signal is for.
points.quote: must use an equally effective method of identifying which crane/derrick the signal is for.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1419, Signals—general requirements (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: "Crane/derrick" includes all equipment covered by Subpart CC.
points.quote: Crane/derrick includes all equipment covered by this subpart.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Related definitions and work area communication

points.text: A qualified evaluator (not a third party) is a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Subpart CC qualification requirements for a signal person.
points.quote: Qualified evaluator (not a third party) means a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated that he/she is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A qualified evaluator (third party) is an entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Subpart CC qualification requirements for a signal person.
points.quote: Qualified evaluator (third party) means an entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated that it is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: To be considered a dedicated spotter (power lines), the requirements of § 1926.1428 (Signal person qualifications) must be met, and his/her sole responsibility is to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories), and ensure through communication with the operator that the applicable minimum approach distance is not breached.
points.quote: Dedicated spotter (power lines): To be considered a dedicated spotter, the requirements of § 1926.1428 (Signal person qualifications) must be met and his/her sole responsibility is to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories), and ensure through communication with the operator that the applicable minimum approach distance is not breached.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Before an employee goes to a location in the hazard area that is out of view of the operator, the employee (or someone instructed by the employee) must ensure that the operator is informed that he/she is going to that location.
points.quote: Before an employee goes to a location in the hazard area that is out of view of the operator, the employee (or someone instructed by the employee) must ensure that the operator is informed that he/she is going to that location.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1424, Work area control (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Where the operator knows that an employee went to a location covered by 1926.1424(a)(1), the operator must not rotate the superstructure until the operator is informed, in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication, that the employee is in a safe position.
points.quote: Where the operator knows that an employee went to a location covered by paragraph (a)(1) of this section, the operator must not rotate the superstructure until the operator is informed in accordance with a pre-arranged system of communication that the employee is in a safe position.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1424, Work area control (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: "Hoisting" is the act of raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by the standard, and it can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.
points.quote: Hoisting is the act of raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by this standard. As used in this standard, “hoisting” can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1401, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

notCovered: Signal person qualification and evaluation requirements (§ 1926.1428) are only named here where the definitions cross-reference them.
